requirement: A self-origin permission question carries tool and summary from the hook, detected_by "hook", and NO options[] — because verbatim option labels exist only in a pane, and a self session has none. options[] is optional everywhere.
why_it_matters: BACKEND-FINDINGS.md §2. The permission hook payload carries a generic message plus tool_input; the real option text ("Yes, and don't ask again for similar commands in …") lives in the tmux pane. origin "fleet" can capture it; origin "self" cannot. A back-end that synthesised a plausible option list would render buttons that type something the user never read. The v1.1 `decision` kind that this finding also names was already REMOVED in v1.3 — folded into `ask` — and stays removed; the surviving half of the fix is that options[] is explicitly optional and evidence-gated.

counterexamples.why: detected_by claims frame evidence ("both") for a session with no pane, and the three labels are therefore guesses. The GUI would render three answer buttons for a dialog it cannot reach, and "Yes, allow all edits during this session" is a consequence the user never actually saw offered. The shape is legal, which is why this rule is asserted rather than schema-encoded.

counterexamples.name: an option with no label
counterexamples.why: When options[] IS present, every entry must carry the on-screen text. A key without a label is a button with nothing to show the user, which defeats the purpose of reading the labels verbatim.
